title: Exploring the use of novel CuZrTi intermetallic compound for extreme conditions
abstract: Abstract                                        The search for structural materials that can maintain stability under high temperature and radiation is essential for fusion energy applications. Motivated by the favorable mechanical and radiation-resistant properties of                     CuZr                     systems, this study investigates a new                     CuZrTi                     intermetallic compound using first-principles density functional theory. The focus of the research is to understand the structural configuration, phase stability, mechanical response, electronic structure, and behavior of helium interstitials. To assess stability and bonding characteristics, we carried out analysis of phonon, elastic, and electron localization. We also evaluated the formation energies of helium to understand its behaviour at interstitial sites. The goal of this investigation is to provide insights into how the presence of                     Ti                     influences the thermodynamic, mechanical, and electronic properties of                     CuZr                     based alloys. This framework aims to guide future applications of these materials in nuclear fusion environments.
